records.place: Abrunhosa do Mato, between Mangualde and Nelas, Dão

wine.name: Quinta dos Roques Touriga Nacional
wine.grapes: Touriga Nacional alone, from the family's own vineyards.
wine.sites: The estate's vineyards around Abrunhosa do Mato on the Dão plateau, at about 450 metres on gentle south facing slopes of sandy granite with schist in places, sheltered by the mountains that ring the region.
wine.making: Made only in years the house judges good enough: the grapes are wholly destemmed and fermented on their skins in stainless steel vats, then the wine is aged for fourteen to seventeen months, by vintage, in 225 litre French oak barrels, new in some years and used in others, and lightly filtered before bottling.
wine.glass: Violet, pine resin and ripe blackberry, with blueberry, bramble and a touch of clove; full and firm, with powerful, juicy tannin held up by fresh acidity.
wine.ageing: Firm and tight when young, it gains from a few years in bottle and keeps for a decade and more in a strong vintage.
wine.serve: 16 to 18 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle an hour ahead; a large red wine glass.

label.means: Quinta means a farm or estate: the wine is grown on the family's own property.
The grape, named on the label because the wine is made from it alone.
The appellation of the granite plateau around Viseu, demarcated by the law of 18 September 1908.

records.table: Quinta dos Roques Touriga Nacional comes from a family estate between Mangualde and Nelas that began bottling the grape alone with the 1996 vintage. Expect violet, pine resin and blackberry over firm, juicy tannin; decant it and pour it with roast lamb.
records.story: The family behind Quinta dos Roques has grown grapes at Abrunhosa do Mato, between Mangualde and Nelas, since the nineteenth century, as the house tells it. The Dão around it was demarcated by the law of 18 September 1908, but from the 1960s and 1970s, as the regional commission itself tells it, volume came before quality and the co-operatives ruled the market. The region's revival came from estates that grew, made and bottled their own wine, and Roques was among them. With the 1996 vintage, by the house's own account, the estate began to bottle reds of a single grape, made only in years it judges good enough, Touriga Nacional among them, and in 1998 it added an Encruzado made alone, the Dão's white grape on its own. The family later took on Quinta das Maias, a higher estate near Gouveia in the foothills of the Serra da Estrela, whose wines carry their own name. For a sommelier the Touriga Nacional of Roques is the grape at home: the variety said to have been born in the Dão, shown on its own from granite, fragrant and firm rather than heavy, and a way to learn what the grape brings to the region's blends.

others.name: Quinta dos Roques Encruzado
others.note: The white of Encruzado alone, about half of it fermented in French oak barrels and stirred on its lees for six months or so, the rest in steel.

others.name: Quinta das Maias
others.note: The family's second estate, higher up near Gouveia under the Serra da Estrela, bottled under its own name.

traps: Quinta dos Roques near Mangualde and Quinta das Maias near Gouveia are two estates of one family with two labels, not one wine.
Quinta dos Roques Touriga Nacional is a Dão red from granite, not a Douro red, though the same grape is grown in both regions.

cards.front: Quinta dos Roques: with which vintage did it first bottle Touriga Nacional on its own?
cards.back: With the 1996 vintage, among its first reds of a single grape; an Encruzado made alone followed in 1998.

cards.front: Where do the vines of Quinta dos Roques Touriga Nacional grow?
cards.back: Around Abrunhosa do Mato between Mangualde and Nelas, at about 450 metres on sandy soils over granite.

report: Searches for this record: 9 of the group's share of 35, one of them on the house's own domain, which returned nothing; one shared with the whole group on the CVR Dão's own domain for the law of 18 September 1908 and the co-operative decades.

The 1996 vintage of the varietal Touriga Nacional rests on Fareham Wine Cellar, the importer Raymond Reynolds and a Philippine merchant's listing (txanton.com.ph); a critic's tasting note calling 1996 the first commercial release was read but is not cited, its address naming a living writer, and the plan's first varietal Touriga Nacional of the Dão is not claimed, since no source says first.

The 1998 Encruzado rests on Raymond Reynolds and The Wine Society, both of which call it the first varietal Encruzado of the Dão; Sogrape says Quinta dos Carvalhais introduced the Dão's first Encruzado in 1992, so neither first is told and the tension is left for the checker.

The plan's why calls the Encruzado barrel fermented: The Wine Society and a Decanter review give about a fifth fermented in oak with its own yeasts and some seven months on lees, so others says partly; one merchant's ten months in barrel is left out.

Left out for want of a second source: the family's third generation, the couple's former careers, the year 1997 for Quinta das Maias (The Wine Society alone among usable sources), the Pessegueiro vineyard, and a merchant's claim that Portugal joined the European Community in 1979 (it joined in 1986) ending the co-operatives' hold.

The barrel months differ by vintage: fifteen months in second use French oak (Wine House Portugal) and seventeen in new barriques (Fareham), so the making gives the span; the glass draws on notes at Portugal Get Wine, the International Wine Challenge and CellarTracker; the altitude of about 450 metres and the sandy soils over granite rest on two merchants' estate notes.

Living names met, none in the fragment's prose: the couple who run the estate and the critic of the 1996 note. The importer's company name Raymond Reynolds is used as a house's name in a source title; if its founder is judged a living person to be kept out of titles, the checker may swap that source for txanton.com.ph.

wine.sites: sandy soils over granite now gentle south facing slopes of sandy granite with schist in places (the house's About page); the 450 metres kept on three accounts.

story: more than a century now since the nineteenth century as the house tells it; the 1996 single grape reds now the house's own account, made only in good years; the family also holds Quinta das Maias now took on, a present holding being volatile.
others[0]: a fifth fermented in oak with its own yeasts now about half in French oak barrels and stirred on its lees six months or so, the rest in steel (the house's sheets of 2017, 2019 and 2022).

questions[1].exp: its importer now the house.
sources: Raymond Reynolds, Wine House Portugal and The Wine Society replaced by the house's About page and its Touriga Nacional and Encruzado sheets.

The first varietal Encruzado: 1998 at Roques by The Wine Society and the importer, 1992 at Carvalhais by Sogrape; neither first is told.
Quinta das Maias's year, 1997, and its wines made at Roques from 1992, rest on a writer's profile and one merchant, so the story gives no year.
The Wine Society's fifth in oak may be true of the 2024; the house's sheets read (2017, 2019, 2022) give half.

wine.name: Quinta da Pellada Carrocel
wine.grapes: Touriga Nacional alone, from old vines in a single small parcel.
wine.sites: One small parcel of old Touriga Nacional at Quinta da Pellada near Seia, on granite at about 500 metres in the shelter of the Serra da Estrela.
wine.making: Made only in years when the parcel gives fruit good enough, the wine is fermented in stainless steel with up to about twelve days on its skins, then aged for eighteen months to two years and more in used French oak barrels of 400 to 500 litres, large enough that the wood frames the wine rather than marking it.
wine.glass: Wild red berries, blackberry and black cherry with violet, resin and a balsamic lift; firm, austere tannin and fresh acidity give it a lean, long line rather than weight.
wine.ageing: Austere and closed when young, it needs several years in bottle to open and is built to keep for well over a decade.
wine.serve: 16 to 18 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for an hour or two; a large red wine glass.

label.means: The name of the wine, drawn from one small parcel of old Touriga Nacional at the estate.
The estate at Pinhanços near Seia where the parcel lies, sister to Quinta de Saes.
The appellation; the Serra da Estrela, where Pellada lies, is one of its seven subregions.

records.table: Quinta da Pellada's Carrocel is Touriga Nacional from one small parcel of old vines on granite under the Serra da Estrela, made only in good years and aged in large used barrels. It is lean, perfumed and firm, so decant it.
records.story: Quinta da Pellada lies at Pinhanços, near Seia, where the Dão climbs towards the Serra da Estrela, and its wine is old: records of the sixteenth century, one of them dated 1527, show the estate paying its tax to the crown in barrels of wine. In time the family's own winemaking lapsed. In 1980 a civil engineer of the family inherited the estate and set out to restore it and to make wine there again. The first label came from the sister estate, Quinta de Saes, with the 1989 vintage, and the wines of Pellada followed. Together the two granite estates became a name used to teach the Dão: altitude, mountain shelter, old mixed plantings and Encruzado as the white, with reds that argue for elegance over weight. Carrocel is the estate's statement on Touriga Nacional: one small parcel of old vines, made only when the year allows and aged in large used barrels so that the wood frames rather than marks the fruit. To a sommelier it shows the grape at its most restrained, perfume and firmness rather than power, and it is the wine to pour beside a fuller Touriga from the Douro schist to show what granite and height do to the same grape.

others.name: Quinta da Pellada Primus
others.note: The white: a field blend of old vines led by Encruzado and Bical, with Cerceal and other grapes planted among them, fermented together.

others.name: Quinta de Saes
others.note: The sister estate's label since the 1989 vintage; its Encruzado is the white a candidate is expected to place.

traps: Carrocel is Touriga Nacional alone from one parcel; Primus, the estate's other wine to know, is a white led by Encruzado.
Quinta da Pellada and Quinta de Saes are sister estates of one family near Seia; Saes carried the first label, with the 1989 vintage.

cards.front: Quinta da Pellada Carrocel: what is in the bottle, and from where?

cards.front: Which sister estate of Quinta da Pellada carried the family's first label, and with which vintage?
cards.back: Quinta de Saes, with the 1989 vintage.

New American oak barriques

report: Searches for this record: 6 of the group's share of 35, beside one shared with the group on the IVV's and the CVR Dão's own domains for the seven subregions and the label terms; no page of the estate's own could be found.

The library record p-alvaro-castro gives the country as Spain and Portugal; both estates are in the Dão, so the country reads wrongly and is reported, not edited. Its Pape and Doda as collaborations with a Douro house were not borne out by the searches, which show Pape as a Pellada red; Pape is left out of others.

The estate is named by its quinta and the living winemaker of the library's producer name is never named; the civil engineer of 1980 is he, described by role. The year 1980 and his inheriting the estate rest on Oleobrigado and Wine Paris; Center of Portugal says he bought it, so the record says inherited with the two.

The record of 1527 rests on Center of Portugal and Wine Paris; Garrafeira Nacional gives about 1570, so the story says records of the sixteenth century, one of them dated 1527. Two generations or one without wine is disputed, so the story says only that it lapsed.

Carrocel's single small parcel rests on two merchants (half a hectare at one, five old selections of the grape at another, the selections left out); its planting year is 1950 in one source and its age forty five, seventy five or eighty five years in others, so no year or age is given.

The ageing: 24 months in used 400 litre French oak at Oleobrigado and another merchant, 18 to 24 months in 400 to 500 litre barrels in the winemaker's notes, 28 months for one vintage and 11 or 12 months in two listings, so the making gives eighteen months to two years and more; fermentation in steel with twelve days of maceration rests on one source and is left out.

The Quinta de Saes first label of 1989 rests on Wine Paris, Oleobrigado and Wine Radar; the Pellada brand's 1992 rests on Wine Radar alone and is left out; the daughter who joined her father rests on one source and is left out. Living names met, none in the prose: the winemaker, his daughter and the Douro partner of the library's note.

changed: wine.making: fermentation in stainless steel with up to about twelve days on the skins added, now on three sheets (Leon and Son, Mistral, Vinogrande).
others[0]: Primus from one high parcel now a field blend of old vines led by Encruzado and Bical, fermented together (Vinogrande, Mistral, Cave Lusa).
sources: Center of Portugal and En Primeur Club replaced by the estate's own history page (1527, the inheriting of 1980) and Leon and Son (the parcel, the steel, the barrels).
open: The estate's terroir summary names Vila Nova de Tazém, the neighbouring parish in Gouveia, while three accounts give Pinhanços, Seia; the record keeps Pinhanços.
Carrocel's planting year (1950 on three sheets) and its age (45 or 85 years) disagree, so neither is given; the Wine Advocate's old clones of Talhão 5 rest on one source.
The barrel months run from eighteen (the winemaker's notes, by the author) to thirty (Mistral's 2018); the record's eighteen months to two years and more holds them.
One guide ties the record of 1527 to Quinta de Saes rather than Pellada; the estate's own page claims it for itself.

wine.name: Quinta dos Carvalhais Encruzado
wine.grapes: Encruzado alone, the Dão's own white grape, from the estate's vineyards.
wine.sites: The estate's own vineyards near Mangualde, on granite soils of the Dão plateau sheltered by the Serra da Estrela and the Caramulo.
wine.making: Fermentation begins in stainless steel, and part of the must, most of it in some vintages, is moved partway through into new French oak barrels, mostly of 225 litres and in some years larger, the rest kept in steel; the wine then rests on its fine lees, stirred, for six to eight months before the two are blended and bottled.
wine.glass: Lemon and lemon peel with a lift of white flowers, a flinty, stony edge and, in riper years, apricot; textured and gently toasted, with a firm line of acidity running through it.
wine.ageing: Lively on release, it gains texture and depth over several years in bottle, as Encruzado is known to do, and can keep for a decade.
wine.serve: 10 to 12 degrees Celsius; no need to decant; a medium white wine glass.

label.means: The Dão's own white grape, named alone because the wine is made from it alone.
The estate near Mangualde that Sogrape bought and planted in 1988.
The appellation of the granite plateau around Viseu, demarcated in 1908.

records.table: Quinta dos Carvalhais Encruzado is Sogrape's white of the Dão's own grape, from its estate near Mangualde, partly fermented in new French oak and stirred on its lees. Lemon, flint and a touch of toast over firm acidity: pour it cool with roast fish.
records.story: Sogrape, the Portuguese wine company, has worked in the Dão since 1957, as it tells its own history. In 1988 it bought Quinta dos Carvalhais near Mangualde and planted its vineyards with the region's own grapes, Touriga Nacional, Alfrocheiro and Encruzado among them, giving the company an estate of its own on the granite of the plateau as the Dão, after decades in which the co-operatives ruled its market, began to turn towards estates that made and bottled their own wine. Encruzado became the estate's calling card: the Dão's own white grape, partly fermented in new French oak and kept on its stirred lees, made to gain with age in bottle. Beside it the estate makes Único, a red made only in some years, of which the 2017 was only the fourth edition. In October of that same year a forest fire reached Mangualde and burnt one of the estate's vineyards, Parcela 45, days after its Alfrocheiro was picked, so its 2017 is a wine that can never be made again. For a sommelier Carvalhais Encruzado is the dependable way to meet the Dão's white grape on a list: lemon and flint over a frame of oak, firm with acidity and able to age, from one of the country's large houses rather than a small grower.

others.name: Quinta dos Carvalhais Único
others.note: The estate's flagship red, made only in some years; the 2017 was its fourth edition.

others.name: Quinta dos Carvalhais Parcela 45
others.note: An Alfrocheiro from a single vineyard lost to the forest fires of 2017, a wine that cannot be made again.

traps: Encruzado is the grape of the Dão, not of Bairrada or Vinho Verde: Quinta dos Carvalhais Encruzado is the Dão's own white grape bottled alone.
Único is the estate's red and made only in some years; the Carvalhais wine a guest is most likely to meet is the Encruzado, a white.

cards.front: Quinta dos Carvalhais: when did Sogrape buy and plant the estate, and where is it?
cards.back: In 1988, near Mangualde; Sogrape had worked in the Dão since 1957.

cards.front: How is Quinta dos Carvalhais Encruzado made?
cards.back: Part of the must goes into new French oak barrels during fermentation, the rest stays in steel; then six to eight months on stirred lees.

questions.q: A guest asks what gives Quinta dos Carvalhais Encruzado its toasty frame. Which step in the cellar explains it?
opts: Part fermented in new French oak barrels
Three years in old chestnut casks
Fermentation on the skins in clay
A year under flor in old butts
questions.exp: Part of the must goes into new French oak barrels during fermentation, which gives the toast; ageing under flor is the way of Jerez, never of a white of the Dão.

questions.q: In which year did Sogrape buy and plant Quinta dos Carvalhais near Mangualde?
questions.exp: Sogrape bought and planted the estate in 1988; 1957 is when the company first came to work in the Dão, and 2017 the year fires took one of its vineyards.

report: Searches for this record: 7 of the group's share of 35, four on Sogrape's own domain (the 1957 and 1988 of its Dão page, the fourth edition of Único with the 2017, the vineyard of Parcela 45 lost to the fires of 2017, the granite).

The making rests on the house's 2016 sheet as its importer Evaton hosts it (seven tenths fermented and matured in new 225 litre French barrels from five coopers), Loja do Vinho (moved into the barrels halfway through fermentation), Liberty Wines (partial fermentation and eight months in French oak), Drinkfinder (six months in oak and steel) and two notes of stirring on the lees; one merchant's order of steps (used oak, then six months in new oak) is left out.

Sogrape's own pages say the estate introduced the Dão's first Encruzado in 1992; two merchants say Quinta dos Roques bottled the first varietal Encruzado in 1998, so neither first is told and 1992 is left out of this record for the checker to settle.

The story's decades of co-operative rule are the region record's words, borne out by the CVR Dão's account of the 1960s and 1970s; the company's founding of 1942 with Mateus Rosé is on its own About us page but is left out to keep the sources to five, and its founder is not named for want of his dates.

The plan's why speaks of the Encruzado fermented partly in new oak, which stands; the region record's dependable Encruzado is taken up in the story. Founded is left empty: 1988 is the year Sogrape bought and planted an estate that was older.

The glass draws on notes read through search (the International Wine Challenge, merchants, and a critic's site that is read and not cited) and keeps only the notes more than one gives (lemon, flint and stone, firm acidity, a textured, gently toasted palate) with white flowers and apricot from one each; a decade of keeping is the Codex region record's own line on Encruzado. Living names met, none in the prose: the estate's winemaker since 2014, her predecessor whose last vintage a merchant's article records, and the family members who lead Sogrape.

changed: wine.making: moved into new 225 litre barrels during fermentation now begun in steel and moved partway into new French oak barrels, mostly 225 litres and larger in some years (Garrafeira Portela, Winestuff, Continente).
questions[0].exp: the 225 litre barrels made new French oak barrels, to agree with the making.
story: Sogrape by its own account helping to renew the region, not found on its pages, now the Dão turning from its co-operatives towards estates (the CVR Dão's own account).
story: the fires of 2017 took Parcela 45 now a fire reached Mangualde in October 2017 and burnt it days after its Alfrocheiro was picked (Sogrape and a merchant's copy of its note).
sources: Liberty Wines replaced by Garrafeira Portela's 2021 sheet.
open: Sogrape's first Encruzado of the Dão in 1992 against Roques's first varietal Encruzado of 1998; neither is told.
Eight months on the lees rests on Liberty Wines and Gota a Gota; most sheets read give about six, so six to eight stands.
The estate's 1957 and 1988 rest on Sogrape's own pages, a house's own dates, with no second account read.

wine.name: Casa de Santar Reserva
wine.classification: Reserva, a traditional mention of Portugal's wine law
wine.grapes: Touriga Nacional, about half, with Alfrocheiro and Aragonez, the Tinta Roriz of the north, in about equal shares for the rest.
wine.sites: The house's vineyards around the village of Santar, near Nelas, on the granite plateau of the central Dão.
wine.making: The grapes are wholly destemmed and fermented at about 26 degrees Celsius with a long maceration on the skins; part of the wine is then aged in French oak barrels, for longer than the house's younger reds, before blending and bottling.
wine.glass: Red cherry and raspberry with a tarry edge, turning towards leather and briar as it ages; fresh and lively, of medium to full weight, with firm tannin made for the table.
wine.ageing: Ready a few years after the vintage, it turns towards leather and briar with age and improves for some years in a cool cellar.
wine.serve: 16 to 18 degrees Celsius, as the house advises; decant a younger bottle briefly; a large red wine glass.

label.means: The house of the village of Santar, an old manor estate with its own vineyards.
A traditional mention for a vintage wine of marked quality, with at least 0.5 per cent more alcohol than the legal minimum.
The appellation of the granite plateau around Viseu, demarcated by the law of 18 September 1908.

records.table: Casa de Santar Reserva is the red of an old manor house in the village of Santar, near Nelas: Touriga Nacional with Alfrocheiro and Aragonez, part aged in French oak. Red cherry and tar over firm tannin; pour it at 16 to 18 degrees with roast kid.
records.story: Santar is a village of manor houses in the heart of the Dão, near Nelas, and Casa de Santar is the wine house of its old estate; by its own account it was founded at the end of the eighteenth century, and it counts some two centuries of making wine. The region around it was demarcated by the law of 18 September 1908, and a decree of 25 May 1910 set the rules for its production and trade. The house has kept its own old wines since 1955, a library of past vintages held in a granite room at a low, steady temperature, as it says, to show how its blends of red and white grapes age. Its emblem is the Vinha dos Amores: the story goes that the village's couples once met there in secret, on a slope since planted with Touriga Nacional and Encruzado. The Reserva is the house's classic Dão red, Touriga Nacional with Alfrocheiro and Aragonez, fermented with a long maceration and part aged in French oak. For a sommelier it tells the Dão's older story, of manor houses and blends of the region's grapes, beside the estates of the 1990s that bottled a single grape alone.

others.name: Casa de Santar Vinha dos Amores Encruzado
others.note: Encruzado from the Vinha dos Amores, the slope above the village planted with Encruzado and Touriga Nacional.

traps: Aragonez on the Casa de Santar label is the grape the north of Portugal calls Tinta Roriz and Spain calls Tempranillo, not a different variety.
Casa de Santar Reserva is a blend, not a varietal: Touriga Nacional leads, with Alfrocheiro and Aragonez beside it, where Roques and Passarella bottle Touriga alone.

cards.front: Casa de Santar Reserva: which three grapes make it?
cards.back: Touriga Nacional, about half, with Alfrocheiro and Aragonez in about equal shares.

cards.front: What does Casa de Santar keep in its granite cellar room, and from when?
cards.back: A library of its own old wines, from 1955 onwards, kept cool and steady to show how they age.

questions.q: A guest asks whether Casa de Santar Reserva is a single grape wine. What is the blend?

Baga with Touriga Nacional and Jaen
Encruzado with Malvasia Fina and Bical
Touriga Franca with Tinta Barroca and Sousão
questions.exp: The house's sheet gives about half Touriga Nacional with a quarter each of Alfrocheiro and Aragonez; Touriga Franca and Tinta Barroca are the grapes of a Douro blend.

questions.q: From which year does Casa de Santar's library of its own old wines begin?
questions.exp: The house keeps old vintages from 1955 onwards in a granite room; 1908 is the year the Dão was demarcated by law and 1910 the year of its first rules of production and trade.

report: Searches for this record: 6 of the group's share of 35, three on the house's own domain (the founding at the end of the eighteenth century, the library of old wines from 1955 in its granite room, the Vinha dos Amores, the Reserva sheet), beside the group's two on the CVR Dão's and the IVV's domains for 1908, 1910 and the meaning of Reserva.

Not borne out and left out: the plan's and the region record's claim that Casa de Santar was among the first houses to bottle estate Dão; no source searched says so, and one merchant's claim that it was the first property of the region to use barriques is left out on one source.

Founded is left empty, as the plan's note asks: the house says the end of the eighteenth century, one guide gives vines from the sixteenth century and a manor of the seventeenth, another winemaking from 1616.

The ownership is left out: one news source tells of Dão Sul, now Global Wines, buying a majority from the family in 2006, but it was not borne out in a second, and the house's partnership is not dated in any page read.

The plan's Condessa de Santar white was found on no page of the house, so others carries the Vinha dos Amores Encruzado instead (twelve months in new French oak and six in bottle on the house's page, not cited for want of room among five sources).

The Reserva sheet read is for the 2017 vintage and gives half Touriga Nacional and a quarter each of Alfrocheiro and Aragonez, fermentation at 26 degrees with total destemming and a long maceration, part in French oak with no months given, and 16 to 18 degrees for serving; one listing calls Alfrocheiro dominant and is left out.

wine.name: Villa Oliveira Touriga Nacional
wine.grapes: Touriga Nacional alone, picked from an old vineyard where many grapes grow together.
wine.sites: A single old field blend vineyard of more than eighty years at the estate, on the slopes of the Serra da Estrela near Gouveia, from which only the Touriga Nacional is picked for this wine.
wine.making: The Touriga Nacional is fermented with its own yeasts in concrete vats, by the merchants' sheets, and left on its skins for about a month after fermentation, then aged for one to two years in 225 litre French oak barrels, much of the wood used, and bottled unfiltered.
wine.glass: Cherry, blackberry and cassis with violet, pepper, leather and liquorice, and a balsamic note; full in body yet fresh and elegant, with balanced acidity and a long finish.
wine.ageing: Firm and closed when young, it needs several years to open and has the structure to keep for well over a decade.
wine.serve: 16 to 18 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for an hour or more; a large red wine glass.

records.table: Villa Oliveira Touriga Nacional is Casa da Passarella's flagship red: Touriga Nacional picked alone from an old mixed vineyard under the Serra da Estrela and aged in French oak. Perfumed with violet and cherry, fresh and long; decant it an hour ahead.
records.story: Casa da Passarella was born in 1892, near the end of the phylloxera crisis, as the house tells it, in the hamlet of Passarella at Lagarinhos near Gouveia, on the slopes of the Serra da Estrela; it is older than the demarcation of the Dão. Villa Oliveira, a name that recalls its founder, was first bottled, by the accounts of the estate's history, in 1893. During the Second World War, by the house's account and the Portuguese press, it sheltered a refugee from Burgundy who had fled the war, a winemaker as the house tells it. In later decades the estate declined, and in 2007 or 2008, as accounts differ, new owners bought it and set about restoring the winery and the vineyards, among them old plantings where many grapes grow mixed together. Villa Oliveira returned with the 2009 vintage, after decades off the market, as the house's flagship line. Its Touriga Nacional is a selection: only that grape is picked from one old field blend vineyard of more than eighty years, then aged in French oak. For a sommelier it is the mountain side of the Dão in one glass, Touriga Nacional from old vines high under the Estrela, perfumed and fresh rather than heavy.

report: Searches for this record: 7 of the group's share of 35, one on the house's own domain (born in 1892 near the end of phylloxera, older than the demarcation, the refugee winemaker of the Second World War, the seven plots, the Vinha Centenária and the 125th year edition).

The plan's building of 1892 is borne out by the house, Essential Algarve, En Primeur Club and Wine House Portugal; the first bottling of Villa Oliveira in 1893 by Essential Algarve and a Wine House Portugal listing; its return with the 2009 vintage by Essential Algarve, Wine House Portugal and Cave Lusa's 2009 sheet.

The founder is not named: he is Joaquim Oliveira Santos Lima in one account and Amand d'Oliveira, back from Brazil, in another, with no dates in either, so the story says only that the name recalls its founder.

The sale is 2007 in two accounts and 2008 in two others, so the story gives both; the owner, his fortune and the winemaker are living and are never named; the restoring of the winery and vineyards rests on Wine House Portugal and Essential Algarve's account of the old vines catalogued, while a Houston blog's winery found in ruins is left out on one source. The plan's note of a vineyard's age: more than eighty years on two merchants' sheets, about ninety on one, so more than eighty.

The making differs by vintage: foot trodden in lagares and aged in older 600 litre French barrels for the 2009 by a writer's own site (read, not cited), concrete vats and a year in 225 litre French oak at Cave Lusa, concrete and French oak at Wine House Portugal, 24 months in used 225 litre barrels at Portugal Get Wine; the record gives concrete in recent vintages and one to two years in French oak, much of it used.

The refuge is told as the house tells it, a winemaker who fled the war; one guide says it sheltered Jewish refugees, which is left out. The glass draws on Wine House Portugal, Vinha and Portugal Get Wine; the labels of stories are the house's Monsieur Helis, O Fugitivo and others on its shop, which the story names only as labels of stories.

The refugee: a Jew from Burgundy by Público, French Jews in flight by a guide; a winemaker by trade only in the house's telling.
The vineyard's age: about eighty years at the 2009 harvest on one sheet, more than eighty on two, about ninety on one.
